wheel.note: Cruiser Corps lists the same 15x5.5 OEM steel wheel for 1958–1990 FJ40, FJ45, FJ55, FJ60, FJ62 and BJ trucks, and advises against tires wider than 10.5 in on it.

max_tire.note: An IH8MUD owner runs them with no problems. 31x10.50R15 is the common choice and looks right at stock height; 33x12.50s won't fit without a lift.
Corsetti's FJ62 setup with an OME steering damper. Corsetti says don't go wider than 10.5 in or taller than 33 in on a factory rim.
35s rub on a 2.5-inch OME kit alone. Owners say the A440F auto and stock gears struggle with 35s.

items.title: Rear lap belt may not retract
items.summary: The rear lap belt can stay partly extended and lock; the fix was a belt guide or sheath. 1988 is the only FJ62 year covered.

items.title: Fuel tank separator welds can crack
items.summary: Heat and load can pressurize the tank and crack its internal welds, leaking fuel; the remedy was an improved tank.

timeline.change: 3F-E fuel-injected 4.0 L introduced; the FJ62G VX lets Toyota sell the Land Cruiser in Japan as a passenger vehicle
US FJ62 replaces the FJ60: 155 hp 3F-E, A440F four-speed automatic, square headlights, plusher cabin
Japanese production ends; the 80 Series replaces it for the 1991 US model year, keeping the 3F-E and A440F
Last FJ62s built in Venezuela, with a carbureted 3F

identify.intro: The FJ62 is the easy 60 to live with, but carbureted Venezuelan trucks and imported HJ61s share its body.

items.head: Engine
items.body: US FJ62s have the fuel-injected 3F-E (155 hp), which was also used in the 1991–92 FJ80. Venezuelan FJ62s built to 1992 used a carbureted 3F.

items.head: Transmission
items.body: US trucks came only with the A440F four-speed automatic. A manual FJ62 has been converted, usually to an H55F.

items.head: Looks
items.body: Square headlights and the facelifted front end set it apart from the round-headlight FJ60.

items.head: JDM VX
items.body: The Japanese-market FJ62G VX launched in 1987. Right-hand-drive VX imports are gray-market, not US trucks.

capability.v: 184 x 70.9 x 68.9 in (L x W x H)

values.intro: FJ62s trade at roughly FJ60 money, with restomods and LS or LT swaps at the top.
values.note: Based on 90 Bring a Trailer sales from January 2025 to October 2026 (median about $30,000). Engine-swapped trucks sold for a median of about $44,000; a TLC 4x4-modified 1990 FJ62 made $98,000.

docs.name: Toyota TIS (Technical Information System)
docs.note: Toyota's subscription service portal for most 1990-and-later North American models. Check whether it includes your FJ62's model year before you pay.

paragraphs: Every US FJ62 is a 1988–90 gasoline automatic. HJ61 turbodiesels, right-hand-drive FJ62G VXs and Venezuelan carbureted FJ62s (built to 1992) are gray-market but now more than 25 years old, measured from the date of manufacture. Corsetti Cruisers warns that California may refuse to register an import without a 50-state-compliant emissions system.

production.intro: The FJ62 was built in Japan from 1987 to 1990, and in Venezuela until 1992.
production.paint: 60 Series colors were Alpine White, Brown, Desert Beige, Freeborn Red and Royal Blue, plus metallic Charcoal Gray, Cognac, Gray-Blue, Rootbeer, Sky Blue and Stardust Silver.
